item.title: Danger signals are outside customer base
item.description: When a corporation starts, its members rush to find customers, to meet their needs, to iterate, to create, to re-invent. As the business grows, they search for more customers with the problem their product/service solves. As their customer base expands, they tailor their solution to their customers needs. If their customers’ needs change, they modify their product to match. One might think this cycle would continue forever. The slow, business-killing changes happen, not among one’s own customer base, but with those who are not even customers - the ‘noncustomer’ (Drucker, referenced by Krames, pg. 95).
